optionReasons.saa-med-266:option:1: It's the closest because the Map state also parallels real invocations — but adds an entire state machine to orchestrate what a row solves: no retry/DLQ natives by message and cost by transition; for simple file fan-out, SQS→Lambda with batch size 1 is the direct drawing.
optionReasons.saa-med-266:option:2: More memory gives more CPU, but 10 files from 12 min in an invocation burst the timeout of 15 — internal parallelism does not multiply the clock.
optionReasons.saa-med-266:option:3: Fargate solves another problem (long jobs) — each file fits in 15 min; the goal is to parallelize, not escape the timeout.

finalJustifications: Because a message per file with batch size 1 does the SQS invoke a Lambda by parallel file — 10 simultaneous executions with retry and DLQ natives of the line.
Because the batch size 1 divide the file into 10 slices processed by the same invocation, which adds the results within the timeout.
Because Event Source Mapping extends the timeout of Lambda for 30 minutes when the origin is SQS, covering the 10 files.
Because SQS group 10 files in a single compressed message, and the Lambda processing in accelerated sequence by batch.

optionReasons.saa-med-271:option:0: Deduplication ID acts in the publication (producer) — does not prevent re-delivery by timeout in consumption; and rowing is not necessary.
optionReasons.saa-med-271:option:1: Long polling reduces empty chicks — has no relation to redelivery by expired visibility timeout.
optionReasons.saa-med-271:option:3: It's the closest because ChangeMessageVisibility actually extends the invisibility and is a valid technique — but requires extra code calling the API during processing, a manual heartbeat; with known duration (~2 min), the direct fix is to configure the Visibility Timeout greater than the processing.

finalJustifications: Because with Visibility Timeout greater than processing (ex.: 5 min), the message becomes invisible throughout the work and the redelivery by timeout disappears.
Because the greatest timeout instructs the SQS confirming receipt at delivery, and message is deleted before processing.
Because the timeout of 5 minutes activates the exact-once mode of the Standard row, ensuring a single delivery per message consumed.
Because Visibility Timeout syncs with the timeout of Lambda automatically, and the two clocks expire together.

optionReasons.saa-med-276:option:0: It's the closest because Expedited recovers in minutes and storage is even cheaper — but Expedited is expensive by GB, has limited capacity (can be unavailable without Provisioned Capacity) and serves small ad hoc restorations; for reliable urgency, Instant Retrieval delivers guaranteed immediate access.
optionReasons.saa-med-276:option:1: Deep Archive Standard Recovery Takes ATATE 12 hours — does not fit in the window of 1-2 required hours.
optionReasons.saa-med-276:option:2: Standard-IA COBRA Retrieval by GB (the claim is wrong) — and the discount of ~57% loses to archive classes in rarely accessed.

finalJustifications: Because Instant Retrieval a file cost (~68% minor) with access in milliseconds — urgent restoration is immediate, paying retrieval only when it occurs.
Because Instant Retrieval keeps a hot cache of the most likely backups of restoration, chosen by ML of itself S3.
Because the Instant Retrieval exempts the recovery rate in emergency restorations declared next to the support of the AWS.
Because the Instant Retrieval replicates the 500 TB for a secondary region, and the restoration reads the nearest copy of the team.

optionReasons.saa-med-278:option:0: It's the closest because after replicating the access turns local in fact — but the REPLECTION itself pays the same cross-region transfer per object, and still doubles the storage cost; moving the consumer to the data region eliminates the transfer without doubling anything.
optionReasons.saa-med-278:option:1: VPC Peering between regions ALSO collects inter-region transfer — there is no free route between regions.
optionReasons.saa-med-278:option:2: Transfer Acceleration is for internet uploads via edge — does not apply (no cheating) traffic between regions of the AWS.

finalJustifications: Why put the Lambda in the region of the bucket zero the account: transfer between services within the same region is free, and nothing needs to be duplicated.
Because the Lambda in the same region accesses the S3 the internal network of the AZ, and the AWS credit the old transfer on the following invoice.
Because the change of region activates the free tier regional transfer, which covers the volume of Athena with monthly leave.
Because Athena starts to deliver the results by reference (poster) S3), and the Lambda read the data without actually transferring them.

optionReasons.saa-med-280:option:0: NAT Mechanism saves on time, but turns gargalo and single point of failure managed by you — and cross-AZ traffic remains paid for.
optionReasons.saa-med-280:option:1: It's the closest because endpoints REALMENTE cut cost of NAT for services AWS — But they don't eliminate '100%': the traffic to the INTERNET (the scenario requirement) continues to require the NAT; the cost cross-AZ some is with a NAT Gateway by AZ and local routes.
optionReasons.saa-med-280:option:2: 'Split-horizon DNS' is not a VPC for this — resolution DNS does not change the data path of NAT.

finalJustifications: Because one NAT Gateway by AZ with local route keeps traffic in AZ itself — the cost cross-AZ is missing and the resilience improves break.
Because the three of us NAT Gateways divide the same fixed monthly rate, and the cost per AZ falls to one third of the original value charged.
Because NAT Gateway local compresses the AZ's own outbound traffic, reducing the GB processed at the volume rate.
Because AZ routes activate the aggregate traffic discount of VPC, applied when each AZ resolves its own output.

optionReasons.saa-med-284:option:0: The SSM Inventory collection CONFIGURATION and installed software — does not analyze use or recommend sizes.
optionReasons.saa-med-284:option:1: It's the closest because the Cost Explorer TEM Rightizing Recommendations — but the allegation is wrong: they are based on just metrics of the CloudWatch and focus cost; performance analysis with ML (CPU, memory, network, disk) and projection by workload is the Compute Optimizer.
optionReasons.saa-med-284:option:2: The Trusted Advisor points out instances SUBUTILIZADAS (low-use check) — does not recommend the ideal type/size by workload.

finalJustifications: Because the Computer Optimizer analyzes with ML the historical metrics CloudWatch — CPU, memory with agent, network and disk — and recommends type and size by workload.
Because Computer Optimizer automatically applies the recommendations in the maintenance window, resizing the approved fleet.
Because the Computer Optimizer tests the workload in parallel instances of various sizes and measures the actual performance of each.
Because Computer Optimizer crosses metrics with the invoice of Cost Explorer, prioritizing higher cost instances by use.

optionReasons.saa-med-288:option:0: It is the closest because it seems logical not to pay for what is not in use — but it is the classic mistake of EBS: volume provided charged per GB/month ANEXADO OR NOT; unsealing does not suspend anything — just delete (or snapshot + delete) closes the cost.
optionReasons.saa-med-288:option:2: Snapshots charge per GB/month in QUALQUER region — cross-region copy only adds transfer cost.
optionReasons.saa-med-288:option:3: Snapshots and unattached volumes also charge — there is no 'courtesy' of free storage in AWS.

finalJustifications: 'Cause the three of them are really charging for it.: EIP disassociated by hour, snapshot by GB/month and volume EBS per GB provided — cleaning orphans is direct economy.
Because the triple charge only happens after 30 days of inactivity, the period of absence AWS can resociate everything.
Because EIP stop collects per hour, but snapshots and orphan volumes are converted into storage credits from S3.
Because only the volume EBS full-size charge; EIP and snapshots pay frozen symbolic fee until final exclusion.

optionReasons.saa-med-289:option:0: False: an Intelligent-Tiering TEM object monitoring rate — 'free for any size' is just the mistake.
optionReasons.saa-med-289:option:1: There is no automatic promotion of small objects to the Frequent Access 'to compensate' — tiering follows access, not size.
optionReasons.saa-med-289:option:3: It is the closest because it is correct that there is a fee and that small objects are disadvantaged — but it is wrong to UNIDADE: the monitoring is charged POR OBJETO, not by GB; so the small object is expensive to monitor, and the right is to keep it in S3 Standard.

finalJustifications: Because monitoring is charged by OBJETO/month: below 128 KB the rate exceeds the tiering economy, and the AWS recommends the S3 Standard for them.
Because monitoring is charged by GB, and small objects are virtually free to follow in Intelligent-Tiering.
Because objects below 128 KB go straight to the hot tier at no cost, and monitoring only goes above that size limit.
Because Intelligent-Tiering exempts the rate of small objects and the snake only of large ones, reversing the logic of efficiency by size.
